drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna list only the two loaves and shewbread as wholly for the priests?
outcomeNote: counterexample answered; the emphatic wording explained

segments.he: וְהָאִיכָּא לוֹג שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע! אִיכָּא מַתְּנוֹתָיו.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «But isn’t there» the «log of oil of a leper» that he brings on the day that he becomes ritually clean, which is given completely to the priests? The Gemara answers: It is not given completely to the priests, as «there are its placements,» when oil is sprinkled seven times “before the Lord” (Leviticus 14:16), and applied to the leper’s right ear, thumb, and big toe (see Leviticus 14:17).

segments.he: וּמַאי ״בָּזוֹ״? לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִמַּאן דְּאָמַר: שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם הַבָּאוֹת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן לִשְׂרֵיפָה אָתְיָין, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן דְּבָזוֹ יִפָּה כֹּחַ כֹּהֲנִים לְעוֹלָם.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And what» is meant when the mishna emphasizes: «And in» the case of those offerings, the power of the priests is greater than the power of the altar? The Gemara answers: This wording serves «to exclude» the opinion «of the one who says: The two loaves that are brought by themselves,» unaccompanied by the requisite two lambs, may not be offered, and instead of being eaten «they go to be burned.» By emphasizing that the two loaves and the shewbread are eaten by the priests and not placed on the altar, the mishna «teaches us that in this» case, «the power of the priests is always greater,» even if the two lambs are not offered with the two loaves.
